answer_full:
The Act prohibits the discrimination of a person on the ground of his/her disability, as stated in section 1(1) [Factsheet Section 1]. A person with disability shall not be discriminated against on the o uuu Aun u uons o uosd Xue q aqes s go puno circumstance [Act cl. 1].

If a body corporate discriminates on this ground, it is subject to a fine of N1,000,000, while an individual is liable to pay a N100,000 fine, face a six months imprisonment term or both, as per section 1(2) [Factsheet Section 1]. A person who contravenes subsection (l) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine of N1,000,000 if a body corporate, and a fine of N100,000 or six months imprisonment or both if an individual [Act cl. 1].

A civil action may also be brought by the person discriminated against, as the Act outlaws discrimination in its totality and under any manner or circumstance [Factsheet Section 1]. Notwithstanding prosecution, conviction or otherwise, the person against whom the crime or wrong is committed may maintain a civil action against the person committing the offence or causing the injury, without prejudice to any conviction or acquittal [Act cl. 1].

In this Act, "discrimination" means differential treatment and its verbs and infinite form, discriminate, to discriminate have the corresponding signification [Act cl. 57]. The Act describes a person with disabilities as one who has a long term physical, mental or sensory impairment that may hinder full and effective participation in society on an equal basis with others [Factsheet Section 1].

question: Are public buildings required to be accessible?
answer_excerpt: Yes, public buildings are required to be accessible. A public building shall be constructed with necessary accessibility aids such as lifts (where necessary), ramps, and any other facility that makes them accessible to and usable by persons with disabilities [Act cl. 4]. A person with disability has the right to access the physical environment and buildings on an equal basis with others [Act cl. 3]. This right of access to public premises guarantees a person with disability a right to access the physical environment and buildings on an equal basis with others [Factsheet Section 3]. This provis...
answer_full:
Yes, public buildings are required to be accessible.

A public building shall be constructed with necessary accessibility aids such as lifts (where necessary), ramps, and any other facility that makes them accessible to and usable by persons with disabilities [Act cl. 4]. A person with disability has the right to access the physical environment and buildings on an equal basis with others [Act cl. 3]. This right of access to public premises guarantees a person with disability a right to access the physical environment and buildings on an equal basis with others [Factsheet Section 3]. This provision is further complemented by sections 4 and 5 of the Bill that require public facilities to be accessible and usable by persons with disabilities [Factsheet Section 3]. Public facilities include road-side walks, pedestrian crossings and special facilities such as elevators, crutches, guide canes, toilet facilities, door protective and re-opening devices [Factsheet Section 3].

Before erecting any public structure, its plan shall be scrutinised by the relevant authority to ensure it conforms with the building code [Act cl. 7]. A government or government agency, body or individual responsible for the approval of building plans shall not approve the plan of a public building if it does not make provision for accessibility facilities in line with the building code [Act cl. 7]. Officers who approve such a plan commit an offence and are liable on conviction to a fine of at least N1,000,000 or a two-year imprisonment term or both [Factsheet Section 7,8].

All public buildings or structures, whether immovable or not, must be modified and accessible to persons with disabilities, including those on wheelchairs, within a five-year transitory period [Factsheet Section 6].

question: What employment protections exist for persons with disabilities?
answer_excerpt: All employers of labour in public organisations shall, as much as possible, have persons with disabilities constituting at least 5% of their employment [Act cl. 29]. Persons with disabilities are guaranteed the right to work and earn a living in a labour market/work environment free from hinderances to employment [Factsheet Section 28]. Employers of labour in public institutions shall have at least 5% of persons with disabilities in their employment [Factsheet Section 28]. Persons and companies who breach this provision are liable on conviction to nominal damages of a minimum of N250,000 payab...
answer_full: All employers of labour in public organisations shall, as much as possible, have persons with disabilities constituting at least 5% of their employment [Act cl. 29]. Persons with disabilities are guaranteed the right to work and earn a living in a labour market/work environment free from hinderances to employment [Factsheet Section 28]. Employers of labour in public institutions shall have at least 5% of persons with disabilities in their employment [Factsheet Section 28]. Persons and companies who breach this provision are liable on conviction to nominal damages of a minimum of N250,000 payable to the affected person when an individual commits the offence, or N500,000 when a company commits the offence [Factsheet Section 28]. Principal officers of a company are also liable to pay N50,000 damages to the affected person with disability [Factsheet Section 28]. The Commission shall make available not less than 5% of the work force to qualified persons with disabilities [Act cl. 38]. Among its functions, the Commission is to make available not less than 5 percent of the work force to persons with disabilities [Factsheet Section 38].

question: Is there a commission for persons with disabilities?
answer_excerpt: Yes, there is a National Commission for Persons with Disabilities [Factsheet Section 31]. It is established under the Presidency [Factsheet Section 31] [Act cl. 31]. The Commission is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal [Act cl. 31]. Its head office is in the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja [Act cl. 31].
answer_full: Yes, there is a National Commission for Persons with Disabilities [Factsheet Section 31]. It is established under the Presidency [Factsheet Section 31] [Act cl. 31]. The Commission is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal [Act cl. 31]. Its head office is in the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja [Act cl. 31].

question: What are the penalties for violating the Act?
answer_excerpt: For violations of the Act: * A body corporate that discriminates against a person with disability is liable to a fine of N1,000,000 [Act cl. 1]. * An individual who discriminates is liable to a fine of N100,000 or six months imprisonment or both [Act cl. 1]. * A body corporate who discriminates on the ground of disability is subject to a fine of N1,000,000 [Factsheet Section 1]. * An individual who discriminates is liable to pay a N100,000 fine, face a six months imprisonment term or both [Factsheet Section 1]. * A person who employs, uses, or involves a person with disability in begging, or p...
answer_full:
For violations of the Act:

*   A body corporate that discriminates against a person with disability is liable to a fine of N1,000,000 [Act cl. 1].
*   An individual who discriminates is liable to a fine of N100,000 or six months imprisonment or both [Act cl. 1].
*   A body corporate who discriminates on the ground of disability is subject to a fine of N1,000,000 [Factsheet Section 1].
*   An individual who discriminates is liable to pay a N100,000 fine, face a six months imprisonment term or both [Factsheet Section 1].
*   A person who employs, uses, or involves a person with disability in begging, or parades them in public with the intention of soliciting for alms, commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine of N100,000 or a term of six months imprisonment or both [Act cl. 16].
*   Persons who violate the prohibition of use of Persons with Disability in soliciting for alms are liable on conviction to a fine of N100,000, a term of 6 months imprisonment or both [Factsheet Section 16].
*   A person, organisation or corporate body in control of a public parking lot who fails to provide for reserved spaces for persons with disabilities commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine of N1,000 for each day of default [Act cl. 12].
*   A person without disability who parks a vehicle in a reserved space for persons with disabilities commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine of N5,000 [Act cl. 12].
*   A person who intentionally obstructs a reserved space for persons with disabilities commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine of N5,000 [Act cl. 12].
*   Notwithstanding prosecution, conviction or acquittal, the person against whom a crime or wrong is committed under the Act may maintain a civil action against the person committing the offence or causing the injury [Act cl. 1].

question: Does the Act cover access to vehicles and transport?
answer_excerpt: Yes, the Act covers access to vehicles and transport. Government transport service providers are mandated to provide lifts, ramps, and other accessibility aids to enhance the accessibility of their vehicles, parks, and bus stops for persons with disabilities, including those using wheelchairs [Act cl. 10]. Every public vehicle must also have functional audible and visual displays of their destination within five years from the commencement of this Act [Act cl. 10]. Transport service providers shall make provisions for lifts, ramps, and other accessibility aids to enhance the accessibility of t...
answer_full:
Yes, the Act covers access to vehicles and transport.

Government transport service providers are mandated to provide lifts, ramps, and other accessibility aids to enhance the accessibility of their vehicles, parks, and bus stops for persons with disabilities, including those using wheelchairs [Act cl. 10]. Every public vehicle must also have functional audible and visual displays of their destination within five years from the commencement of this Act [Act cl. 10].

Transport service providers shall make provisions for lifts, ramps, and other accessibility aids to enhance the accessibility of their vehicles, parks, and bus stops to persons with disabilities, including those on wheelchairs [Act cl. 11]. Lifts, ramps, and all other accessibility equipment in or for vehicles, and at parks or bus stops, shall be maintained in operational condition [Act cl. 11]. There shall be regular and frequent maintenance of all accessibility aids and equipment, and defective ones shall be promptly repaired or replaced [Act cl. 11]. Before a person with disability boards or alights from a vehicle, the driver must ensure that the vehicle comes to a stop [Act cl. 11]. When a person with disability intends to board a vehicle, all other intending passengers shall wait for them to board before them [Act cl. 11]. These provisions are also summarized in the factsheet, which states that Section 10 mandates government providers to make provisions for lifts, ramps, and other accessibility aids that enhance the accessibility of their vehicles, parks, and bus stops to persons with disabilities, and every public vehicle to have functional audible and visual display of their destination within five years of commencement of this Act [Factsheet Section 10,11]. A similar provision to section 10(1) is provided in section 11 for all transport service providers [Factsheet Section 10,11]. Section 11 also mandates the regular and frequent maintenance of accessibility aids and equipment in vehicles [Factsheet Section 10,11]. Additionally, section 11(4) places a duty of care on a driver who must ensure that his vehicle comes to a stop before a person with disability alights from the vehicle [Factsheet Section 10,11]. There is also a responsibility placed on all intending passengers to wait for a person with disability to board before them in section 11(5) [Factsheet Section 10,11].

question: What rights do children with disabilities have to education?
answer_excerpt: Children with disabilities have an unfettered right to education without discrimination or segregation in any form [Act cl. 17]. This entitles a person with disability to a right to education free from discrimination [Factsheet Section 17,18]. A person with disability is entitled to free education to secondary school level [Act cl. 17] and free education up to secondary level [Factsheet Section 17,18]. The education of persons with disabilities, especially children, is to be communicated in the most appropriate language and mode, irrespective of whether they are blind, deaf, or with multiple d...
answer_full:
Children with disabilities have an unfettered right to education without discrimination or segregation in any form [Act cl. 17]. This entitles a person with disability to a right to education free from discrimination [Factsheet Section 17,18]. A person with disability is entitled to free education to secondary school level [Act cl. 17] and free education up to secondary level [Factsheet Section 17,18].

The education of persons with disabilities, especially children, is to be communicated in the most appropriate language and mode, irrespective of whether they are blind, deaf, or with multiple disabilities [Factsheet Section 20].

The Commission shall provide educational assistive devices [Act cl. 17]. The National Commission for Persons with Disabilities is mandated to provide educational assistive devices [Factsheet Section 17,18].

All public schools from primary to tertiary are mandated to be inclusive of and accessible to persons with disabilities [Factsheet Section 17,18]. To achieve this, these schools are mandated to provide special facilities and at least one trained personnel to cater for the education of persons with disabilities in every school [Factsheet Section 17,18]. Braille, sign language, and other skills are mandated to form part of the curricula in primary, secondary, and tertiary institutions [Factsheet Section 17,18]. The Commission's functions include establishing and promoting inclusive schools, vocational, and rehabilitation centres for the development of persons with disabilities [Act cl. 38].

The education of special education personnel shall be highly subsidised [Act cl. 19]. This provision for subsidised education for special education personnel compliments the right to free education and inclusiveness [Factsheet Section 19,17].

The Commission's functions include facilitating the procurement of scholarship awards for persons with disabilities up to university level [Act cl. 38]. These functions also include facilitating the procurement of scholarships awards for persons with disabilities up to university level [Factsheet Section 38].

question: How long is the transitional compliance period?
answer_excerpt: The transitory period is five years [Factsheet Section 6]. There shall be a transitory period of five years from the date of the commencement of the Act [Act cl. 6].
answer_full: The transitory period is five years [Factsheet Section 6]. There shall be a transitory period of five years from the date of the commencement of the Act [Act cl. 6].

question: Does the Constitution guarantee dignity and equality?
answer_excerpt: Yes, the Constitution guarantees dignity and equality. Every individual is entitled to respect for the dignity of his person [Constitution s. 34]. The State social order is founded on ideals of Freedom, Equality and Justice [Constitution s. 17]. Also, every citizen shall have equality of rights, obligations and opportunities before the law [Constitution s. 17], and the sanctity of the human person shall be recognised and human dignity shall [Constitution s. 17].
answer_full: Yes, the Constitution guarantees dignity and equality. Every individual is entitled to respect for the dignity of his person [Constitution s. 34]. The State social order is founded on ideals of Freedom, Equality and Justice [Constitution s. 17]. Also, every citizen shall have equality of rights, obligations and opportunities before the law [Constitution s. 17], and the sanctity of the human person shall be recognised and human dignity shall [Constitution s. 17].

question: Where can I get legal aid for a disability rights violation?
answer_excerpt: An indigent citizen of Nigeria may receive financial or legal aid to engage the services of a legal practitioner to prosecute their claim where their right has been infringed [Constitution s. 46]. The functions of the Commission include receiving complaints of persons with disabilities on the violation of their rights [Act cl. 38]. The Commission also supports an individual's right to seek redress in court, investigation, prosecution or sanctioning, in appropriate cases, for the violation of the provision of the Act [Act cl. 38]. Among its functions, the Commission is also responsible for rece...
answer_full: An indigent citizen of Nigeria may receive financial or legal aid to engage the services of a legal practitioner to prosecute their claim where their right has been infringed [Constitution s. 46]. The functions of the Commission include receiving complaints of persons with disabilities on the violation of their rights [Act cl. 38]. The Commission also supports an individual's right to seek redress in court, investigation, prosecution or sanctioning, in appropriate cases, for the violation of the provision of the Act [Act cl. 38]. Among its functions, the Commission is also responsible for receiving complaints by persons with disabilities on violation of their rights [Factsheet Section 38].
